assessment.nobel_worthiness: A clear discovery from nature: the first high-energy astrophysical neutrinos, opening neutrino astronomy as a new window on the most violent cosmic accelerators. The result stands on observation, which is exactly what I want the prize to reward, and it has an obvious existential and astrophysical appeal.
assessment.attribution: Halzen is the intellectual driver of the IceCube concept and its long realisation, so a single-laureate configuration is defensible from the supplied credit. I recognise that a large collaboration, and earlier pioneers of the detector idea, make the allocation a judgement the committee would need to probe with outside experts.
assessment.maturity: The diffuse flux was seen in 2013 and has been reinforced by later analyses, including the TXS 0506+056 coincidence and galactic-plane neutrinos. Source identification is still partial, but the discovery itself is well confirmed and the timing is reasonable.
uncertainties: Whether a single credited name can fairly represent a collaboration-scale discovery.
Origin of most of the diffuse flux is still unresolved, so the astrophysical interpretation is incomplete.
I am relying on memory of the IceCube history and have not verified who proposed what.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Theory predicted flat bands at a magic twist angle, and experiment then found correlated insulators and superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene. Prediction followed by confirmation in nature is the pattern I value, and it launched an entire field of moire quantum materials.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the decisive theoretical prediction and Jarillo-Herrero's group made the decisive experimental discovery, which gives a natural theory-plus-experiment trio. Eva Andrei and others contributed important early experimental work, so the cut is not without contention.
assessment.maturity: Independently reproduced in many laboratories within a few years, with a broad and still-growing body of follow-up. Some interpretive questions about the superconducting mechanism remain open, but the core discovery is secure.
uncertainties: Unresolved microscopic mechanism of superconductivity in the magic-angle system.
Credit for earlier experimental evidence of flat bands and for the Andrei group's contributions.
Whether the field is still too young for the committee to feel the choice is obvious.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Inflation addresses the horizon and flatness problems and, crucially, explains the quantum origin of the primordial fluctuations that seed structure. The near scale-invariant, adiabatic and Gaussian spectrum measured in the CMB is a real clue from nature that supports the framework. I also know the trans-Planckian questions around it from my own work, so I am aware of its limits.
assessment.attribution: Guth and Linde on the mechanism and Mukhanov on the quantum generation of perturbations is a coherent trio from the supplied names. The list does not include Starobinsky or Albrecht and Steinhardt, whose contributions are historically significant, so the allocation is contested.
assessment.maturity: The generic predictions are confirmed to high precision, but no primordial gravitational-wave signal has been found, and the specific inflationary model remains undetermined. I would want the experts to say whether the prize would honour the mechanism or only the structure-formation prediction.
uncertainties: Absence of a primordial B-mode detection leaves the inflationary mechanism itself not directly tested.
Priority disputes (Starobinsky, Kazanas, Sato and others) complicate fair attribution.
Whether the evidence supports inflation specifically or only a broader class of early-universe scenarios.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: A conceptually deep new class of matter with protected edge or surface states, predicted by theory and realised experimentally in HgTe quantum wells and in bismuth-based three-dimensional materials. It is original, clear and has had lasting influence across condensed matter physics.
assessment.attribution: Kane's theory (with Mele) of the quantum spin Hall state, Molenkamp's experimental observation, and Hasan's observation of three-dimensional topological insulators form a plausible triple. Excluding Mele and the other early theorists (Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang) is a real allocation problem.
assessment.maturity: Thoroughly confirmed by many groups and well past the point of doubt. Because the 2016 prize already recognised topological phase transitions, the committee must judge whether this is a distinct enough discovery.
uncertainties: Overlap with the topological theme of the 2016 prize and with the related candidates on this longlist (B029, B045).
Many contributors (Mele, Bernevig, Zhang, Moore, Fu, Balents) make a three-person limit awkward.
I am not myself a condensed-matter specialist and would rely on expert reports.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The discovery of X-ray and optical afterglows settled the long-standing question of the distance and origin of gamma-ray bursts, showing they are cosmological and tied to the deaths of massive stars. This is a clean observational discovery that changed the field, with an existential flavour about the most energetic explosions known.
assessment.attribution: BeppoSAX's localisation (Costa, Frontera) and the follow-up optical redshift work (Kulkarni's group) are decisive links in the chain. Other groups, such as van Paradijs and the optical and radio teams, also have a strong claim, so the credit is not tidy.
assessment.maturity: Fully established for more than two decades and strengthened by supernova associations and gravitational-wave plus gamma-ray burst events. It is mature, perhaps overdue.
uncertainties: Competing priority claims among the BeppoSAX, optical and radio discoverers.
Whether the committee sees it as astronomy more than physics.
My memory of the 1997 chronology may be imperfect.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultracold atoms in optical lattices realise clean, tunable many-body Hamiltonians, from the Mott-insulator transition to quantum gas microscopy, and so serve as true quantum simulators. Zoller supplied the theoretical blueprint, and the experiments gave genuine tests of ideas from condensed matter.
assessment.attribution: Zoller (theory, with Cirac and Jaksch) plus the Bloch and Greiner experimental lines gives a sensible grouping, although Esslinger and Cirac also have strong claims. The set of five credited names exceeds what a prize can hold and the cut will be debated.
assessment.maturity: Mature and broadly confirmed, with the field now moving toward applications. The 2001 and 2012 prizes already recognised parts of the cold-atom story, so novelty needs to be argued.
uncertainties: Overlap with earlier cold-atom and quantum-information prizes.
Fair division of credit between lattice theory and quantum gas microscopy.
Whether the physics learned is a new discovery or mainly a technique.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Evidence for a nanohertz gravitational-wave background is a new window on the Universe, probably from supermassive black-hole binaries, and ties directly to gravitation, which is close to my own field. It is an observation-led discovery from nature.
assessment.attribution: The result comes from several large collaborations (EPTA, NANOGrav, PPTA, CPTA, InPTA) with decades of pulsar-timing groundwork, so naming three people is hard. The supplied names look like leaders of regional efforts, and the pulsar-timing method's originators may also deserve credit.
assessment.maturity: The 2023 evidence is statistically significant but not yet at the discovery threshold in the usual sense, and the interpretation, whether black-hole binaries or new physics, is not settled. I would consider the recognition premature.
uncertainties: Source of the background is not established; cosmological alternatives remain possible.
Significance of the correlation (Hellings-Downs) signal is still moderate.
Collaboration structure makes any small laureate set arbitrary.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The measurement of a sizeable theta13 completed the three-flavour mixing picture and made leptonic CP violation experimentally accessible. It is a precise, unambiguous observation, though it fills in a parameter rather than overturning an idea.
assessment.attribution: Daya Bay (Wang, Luk) gave the decisive high-significance reactor result, while T2K (Nishikawa) provided the accelerator appearance evidence. Double Chooz and RENO also contributed, so three names leave a fair-credit problem.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by several independent experiments and now a precision parameter. The 2015 prize already honoured neutrino oscillations, which weakens the case for another neutrino-mixing prize.
uncertainties: Whether this adds enough to the 2015 neutrino-oscillation prize.
Division of credit among Daya Bay, T2K, RENO and Double Chooz.
I am working from memory on the exact sequence of announcements.
